<reason>B won the comparative frame: prioritization is not abandonment, existing channels remain, and marginal spending should create first encounters where youth actually are. B also neutralized the creator-incentive attack, answered the broken-funnel point with sequenced depth, and showed channel expansion is at least as cannibalistic of journalism budgets. A defended depth and universality forcefully but repeatedly conflated expansion with necessary maintenance and never explained how more linear channels create youth familiarity or trust.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: partnerships need not be per-engagement, hiring creators would destroy their independent community value, and short-form can multiply existing investigations at lower marginal cost than filling another channel.</best_rebuttal>
